flags.title: Band 6 `tc` is mislabelled in the file's own tags
flags.evidence: The GeoTIFF tags say `tc` = 'Tilt angle or total curvature - magnetic field derivative' (data_category magnetic_data). Numerically it correlates r = +0.997 with the external USGS GeoDAWN radiometric TOTAL COUNT channel and r = +0.013 with a computed magnetic tilt angle; all values are positive (2.95 to 88.6) while a tilt angle spans both signs. The DrivenData page figure caption also calls it total radiometric counts.
flags.action: Treat `tc` as radiometric total count (surface lithology/soil), not a magnetic edge detector. Earlier hypotheses that assumed a magnetic meaning were mis-specified (numerically harmless, conceptually wrong).

flags.title: Bridged sample_submission.tif is not an all-absence template
flags.evidence: The official page says the sample 'predicts total fault absence'. The bridged file (SHA-256 2176d08e...) has 60,988 pixels = 1.0 that equal the known-fault mask exactly; everything else in the footprint is 0. The login-gated data tab cannot be fetched here, so the authoritative original was not compared.
flags.action: Do not use it as a zero baseline. Only its footprint/grid are relied upon (verified equal to the labels footprint and to the GeoDAWN area). Ask DrivenData support whether the file differs from the data-tab download.

flags.title: Dropbox links in the request are personal shares, not official hosting
flags.evidence: The Dropbox previews show 'Jason shared this file'. They are not hosted by DrivenData, DOE, NLR or USGS, and their bytes could not be fetched here.
flags.action: Use them only as convenience copies. Authoritative data: the DrivenData data tab (login) and the official rules PDF/GDR links in the sources table.

flags.title: labels.tif provenance independently verified against the official GDR data
flags.evidence: GDR INGENIOUS Quaternary Faults v1 and v2 (DOI 10.15121/1881483), rasterised on the EPSG:32611 100 m grid, reproduce 60,958 of the 60,988 bridged label pixels exactly (99.95 %); 100 % are within 1 px. v1 and v2 are identical on this grid.
flags.action: No action. Keep the CI job to re-check after any data change.

flags.title: Every feature band has invalid pixels INSIDE the scored footprint
flags.evidence: Each of the 19 bands carries the sentinel -3.4028235e38 on 3,061 footprint pixels (3,073 for `tc`) and has 1,540 valid pixels outside the footprint. Any raster-wide model or filter that propagates NaN will write NaN into the submission.
flags.action: Fill holes before modelling and always sanitise predictions (NaN -> 0, clip to [0, 1]). gems.submission.write_submission does this; the browser checker flags any NaN inside the footprint.

flags.title: Earlier README/register said the catalogue-masking rule was unconfirmed
flags.evidence: DrivenData staff confirmed it in forum topic 11516 (posts 2 and 4): known-fault pixels are masked pixel-exactly in both rounds, and no buffer applies to known faults.
flags.action: Documentation updated; src/gems/metric.py cites the verified posts.

flags.title: The 0.3049 top score in the request was stale
flags.evidence: Snapshot (2026-09-30, re-read 02:27 UTC): rank 1 DARD 0.3168, rank 2 alexoktaba 0.3042. Scores and ranks move within hours; the snapshot is not a feed.
flags.action: Open the live leaderboard before decisions.

flags.title: Group entries appear under separate DrivenData accounts
flags.evidence: The public leaderboard lists SDCF9, smashi34, wbg1 and smrtdoog5 (named by the owner) and extradr19 (identical 0.1563, NOT named by the owner) as separate accounts. DrivenData's Terms of Use say accounts are personal; the rules give one final submission per entity and three uploads per week.
flags.action: Confirm that these are distinct eligible individuals or register one team. Do not pool accounts to multiply the weekly limit. Ask gemsprize@nlr.gov if unsure.

flags.title: An automatic leaderboard/forum feed would violate DrivenData's Terms of Use
flags.evidence: Terms of Use, Prohibited Uses: users agree not to use any robot, spider or other automatic device to access the website, including for monitoring or copying.
flags.action: No scraper is included. The 'feed' covers official open-data hosts (GDR, USGS) and the team's own GitHub repos; leaderboard snapshots are taken by a person. Consider asking info@drivendata.org for written permission first.

flags.title: Generative-AI use must be disclosed in any prize narrative
flags.evidence: Official rules section 3.2 requires disclosing the extent and manner of generative-AI use.
flags.action: Record AI assistance in the eventual solution documentation; this repository was developed with AI coding agents.

flags.title: Reference notebook output differs from the stated file spec
flags.evidence: It writes dtype=y_final.dtype (float64 as written), with no nodata and no NaN outside the footprint, whereas the page asks for float32 and NaN outside. The platform still presumably accepts it, which suggests the checker is tolerant of finite-everywhere files.
flags.action: Informational. Our files follow the page text and the official sample's raster profile.

flags.title: GeoDAWN magnetic products have anisotropic resolution
flags.evidence: Area 2 (most of the extent) was flown with 400 m east-west lines. Cross-line (north-south) sampling is coarse, so E-W lineaments in 100 m magnetic derivatives may be flight-line or levelling artefacts (inference, untested).
flags.action: Down-weight purely E-W magnetic lineaments unless corroborated by topography.

flags.title: 'Predicted values must be in range [0, 1]' cannot be reproduced from any file in this repository
flags.evidence: Every file ever published on this site (including the ZIPs and the versions from PR #1) passes all check variants: float32, finite 0-1 on every footprint pixel, correct grid. The repositories behind scored group entries publish files in every encoding (LZW/deflate, predictor 1/3, striped/tiled, NaN or zero outside), so the container is unlikely to be the cause (assuming the published file is what was uploaded). The likeliest causes are NaN or out-of-range values in a file from elsewhere, or server behaviour we cannot see.
flags.action: Run the suspect file through the checker on the Submit page; if it passes but is rejected, email info@drivendata.org with the filename, SHA-256 and a screenshot.

flags.title: SGMC geologic-map faults are coarse and a newer release exists
flags.evidence: SGMC is nominally 1:1,000,000 (positions may be hundreds of metres off), and USGS marks a 2026 re-release (doi 10.5066/P1A3DQZK). The state shapefiles from mrdata were used; their exact version was not pinned.
flags.action: Pin the version before relying on it; treat results as exploratory.

flags.title: Earlier downloads (a16f01, b16f02, c16f03) were unvalidated composites
flags.evidence: They contained up to 148,000 pixels taken from ens12 plus hand-chosen additions, never passed the holdout gate, and the NaN/all-finite pair carried the same prediction.
flags.action: Retired to docs/archive/ (kept for audit). New candidates are built by scripts/build_candidates.py with recorded validation.

flags.title: H18-3a passed the pre-registered gate, but a control explains most of the lift
flags.evidence: A plain fault-density prior yields sparse 0.0931 vs 0.0940 for the endpoint/junction prior (5 re-drawn proxies: means 0.0975 vs 0.0995 vs 0.0866 baseline). The random-20%-components proxy rewards fault clustering by construction.
flags.action: Describe it as a clustering prior with a small structural increment, not as a validated structural-setting mechanism.

flags.title: The holdout measures known faults; the real task scores NEW faults
flags.evidence: Known faults are masked in the real scoring, so the dense proxy rewards something the evaluator ignores, and both proxies' hidden faults are Quaternary catalogue faults. Measured: across the group's 15 distinct scored files the dense known-fault DTI has Spearman rho +0.17 (p = 0.54) with the public score, and the SGMC-gap truth +0.52 (p = 0.048); neither is a dependable gate.
flags.action: Treat holdout numbers as weak evidence; use the first live A/B pair to recalibrate (decision rules in the register, section 6b).

flags.title: H16-1's blend weights may have been chosen on the same holdout
flags.evidence: The 0.55/0.35/0.06/0.04 (lidar) and 0.40/0.35/0.15/0.10 (gap) weights are hard-coded in the prior script; how they were chosen is undocumented, so H16-1's holdout score may be optimistically biased against fresh hypotheses.
flags.action: Prefer fixed-form, pre-registered comparisons; re-tune only on folds that never see the test quadrant.

flags.title: Four of 18 scored entries are effectively one submission
flags.evidence: GEMSDOE1, 5GEMSDOE and 8GEMSDOE are identical on every scored pixel (first two byte-identical); GEMSDOE2 is a 0.946-Jaccard near-duplicate (LB 0.1560). Three more repos (6GEMSDOE, 11GEMSDOE, GEMSDOE10-H16) independently tried near-catalogue predictions and all scored <= 0.046.
flags.action: Run the uniqueness gate on every candidate; do not upload anything with Jaccard >= 0.80 to a scored file.

flags.title: Metric-implementation assumption checked: predictions on masked known-fault pixels
flags.evidence: Our evaluator let predictions on masked known-fault pixels earn true-positive credit (neutral only for false positives); the staff wording implies they should not score at all. Re-scoring six sparse proxies with those predictions dropped changed any arm's mean sparse DTI by at most 0.0001 and left every conclusion unchanged (H18-3a beats H16-1 and the density control in 6/6 draws).
flags.action: None. Both rules are implemented (`mask_predictions`); the candidate files contain no predictions on known-fault pixels.

flags.title: Recorded build commit aa504ca8f1 no longer exists; a sandbox restore corrupted one binary file
flags.evidence: Between sessions the agent sandbox was restored from a file snapshot onto a fresh clone, so the local-only git commits made after the last push were lost and the commits in the published pull request were re-created from the restored working tree (the pre-registration commit 6c5f74a was already on the remote branch and is unchanged; its file is byte-identical). Two generated files, docs/data/submissions.json and evidence/submission_validation_report.json, still record the pre-restore build commit aa504ca8f1, which does not exist in the published history. The restore also corrupted docs/data/footprint.bin (found text-decoded with U+FFFD replacement bytes: 31,029 bytes instead of 15,681); tests/test_footprint.py caught it. After the restore all 9 published files in docs/downloads/ were re-hashed and matched their recorded SHA-256 and sizes.
flags.action: footprint.bin was regenerated from the official template (sha256 2176d08e...) and is byte-identical to the recorded payload (sha256 9ec93feb..., docs/data/footprint.json unchanged). Integrity is anchored on content hashes, not commit ids: the git_commit field in those two JSON files is informational (no page or test reads it) and is refreshed the next time scripts/build_candidates.py runs. If tests/test_footprint.py fails again after a restore, rebuild the payload as described in AGENTS.md.

flags.title: Candidate #3 (SGMC geologic-map faults) repeats an idea the group already built: Jaccard 0.63 with an unregistered GEMSDOE3 file
flags.evidence: The first real run of scripts/scan_group_repos.py (2026-09-30) cross-checked our three ready-to-upload candidates against the 42 published GeoTIFFs in the group repositories that are not in the registry. #1 (H18-3a) and #2 (H16-1) are clear of all of them (most similar: GEMSDOE2 gemsdoe2-extension-arm-ad5ba911.tif, Jaccard 0.07). #3 shares 46,198 of its 57,783 scored positive pixels with GEMSDOE3/docs/downloads/gapfinder-v2-sgmc-gap-20260925T045014Z-7251c22bb4.tif (61,664 positives): Jaccard 0.6307, below the 0.80 duplicate threshold but far above every other pair. GEMSDOE3's README describes SGMC-gap traces as an input to its Gapfinder and Coverline work ('Coverline v3 fusion ... + SGMC-gap traces') and says its current portfolio is unscored ('No upload has been made'). Whether the gapfinder file was ever uploaded is not known: it is not in the registry and no score is recorded for it. Earlier wording in the hypothesis register ('uses an independent official map', 'the most different candidate from every registered file') was true of the 21 registered files only; it has been corrected.
flags.action: Treat #3 and GEMSDOE3's gapfinder-v2-sgmc-gap file as one experiment and upload at most one of them, and only if you want to measure whether geologic-map faults are what the experts added (it cannot pass the holdout gate). Prefer uploads #1 and #2. From now on group-scan cross-checks every ready-to-upload candidate against newly published group files, and the result is shown on each candidate card.

flags.title: Why 17GEMSDOE-F scored 0.0187 (300m halo memorization) and 18GEMSDOE scored 0.0297 (8.76% footprint over-prediction)
flags.evidence: Pixel-level audit of newly reported leaderboard scores: (1) 17GEMSDOE-F (0.0187 LB) placed 61.5% of its 90,746 scored pixels within 300 m of existing catalogued faults and only 1.6% beyond 1.5 km (repeating the failure mode of 6GEMSDOE 0.0286, which placed 68.2% within 300 m). Because DrivenData masks known catalogued faults pixel-exactly with no buffer (Forum Topic 11516 Post 4), hugging the 300 m collar around known faults misses off-catalogue new faults. (2) 18GEMSDOE (0.0297 LB) emitted 452,798 scored positive pixels (8.76% of the entire footprint, 3.6x the 2.45% power-law hidden-fault prior) AND set all 60,988 known faults to 1.0, flooding the DTI denominator with false-positive penalty alpha * FP_w ~= 90,560. By contrast, 16GEMSDOE (0.1855 LB) and 19GEMSDOE-H19-4 (0.1894 LB) emitted ~2.40% of the footprint (~123,800 pixels) with ~19.8% <=300 m and ~49.5% >1.5 km.
flags.action: Enforce the power-law hidden-fault prior budget (~2.40%-2.50% of footprint) and verify spatial distance profile (~20% <=300 m, ~50% >1.5 km) before promoting any candidate.

flags.title: All prior repos (GEMSDOE1-19GEMSDOE) used naive PN binary cross-entropy on PU-contaminated labels.tif
flags.evidence: In existing_faults.tif (labels.tif), s=1 (60,988 pixels, pi_P = 0.011803) is positive, but s=0 (5,106,385 pixels) is UNLABELED (containing ~126,599 hidden positive fault pixels, pi_hidden = 0.024500, total class prior pi = 0.036303, labeling frequency c = pi_P / pi = 0.3251; for short faults L in [300 m, 1,650 m), c(L) = 0.0678). Standard PN training treats s=0 as clean negative y=0, which penalizes the model whenever it predicts high probability on an unmapped fault in U and compresses raw probabilities downward (pre-calibration Murphy Brier Reliability error REL = 0.019674, ECE = 0.13277).
flags.action: Implemented Kiryo et al. (NeurIPS 2017) Non-Negative PU (SAR-nnPU) risk estimator in src/gems/pu_learning.py and Out-of-Fold PU-Isotonic calibration in src/gems/calibration.py, reducing Murphy Reliability error REL by 99.3% (0.019674 -> 0.000143) and ECE by 96.9% (0.13277 -> 0.00405) on held-out fault corridors.
flags.how_established: computed in 20GEMSDOE PU & Brier calibration audit
